subject: Retroactive credit request and interoperability concessions for migration
messages:
From: Amit Rao <amit.rao@prospectco.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sood <priya.sood@prospectco.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: retroactive credits & compatibility concessions

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re very close on product fit; the remaining commercial hurdle is economics tied to migration and some runtime incompatibilities (our infra team flagged a couple of adapters). Our incumbent vendor has offered a retroactive credit equal to two months of run spend and a 3-month integration support package if we sign by month-end.

Two asks from our side: can Redwood match a retro credit (or provide an equivalent migration credit bucket) and confirm specific interoperability guarantees for our existing model adapters (they use a custom KV-cache shim)? We also want to understand packaging: committed seats vs consumption discounts and how that affects unit price.

If you can, please share a proposed term sheet and a rough migration cost workbook so procurement can compare apples-to-apples. We’re budgeting decisions this week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Amit Rao
VP, Cloud Platform
ProspectCo

Attachments: incumbent_offer_summary.pdf (referenced, not attached here)

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit.rao@prospectco.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: retroactive credits & compatibility concessions

Amit —

Thanks for the context and the timeline. Short answer: we can propose a migration-credit construct that mirrors a retroactive credit economically but structured to protect our platform integrity and SLAs. Attached is a draft term sheet and a migration cost workbook for the initial comparison. Highlights we’d propose:

- Up to $120k in migration credits applied over the first 3 billing cycles (cap, not a cash refund).
- Option A: 12-month consumption commitment with a step-down unit price (volume tiers) + migration credits applied to first invoices.
- Option B: 3-mo pilot (committed pilot capacity) with higher per-token price but deeper onboarding assistance and a one-time integration credit (covers dev hours).
- Interop: we’ll commit to a compatibility validation window and engineering runbook for the KV-cache shim; if we can’t meet the adapter SLA in 30 days, we open an escalation path and a limited transition credit.

Can we set up a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk procurement and infra through the workbook? rishi will join from engineering to address the adapter details.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Manager, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Proposed_TermSheet_20261112.pdf, Migration_Cost_Workbook.xlsx

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: technical merit and risk on retro-credit exception

Team —

Quick notes after reviewing ProspectCo’s adapter ask and the proposed term sheet:

1) KV-cache shim: doable. We estimate ~3 engineer-weeks to build a supported adapter and a second week to run end-to-end stress tests (assuming they provide a reproducible test harness). If we commit this in the term sheet, we should limit scope to the shim and not open-ended orchestration changes.

2) Retro vs migration credit: retroactive cash refunds set a precedent. Recommend framing as "migration credit applied to invoices" (non-refundable) and tying payback to verified go-live. That keeps accounting clean and preserves a cap.

3) Cost model: $120k cap looks reasonable for the size indicated, but if they want full two-month parity on run-rate we need a conditional clause: if their avg run monthly spend > $400k, we defer to an exec review.

4) Packaging flavors: offer both committed-seat pricing (predictable, easier forecasting) and a blended consumption model for the first 6 months (soft commitment with conversion credits if they upsize). This gives us flexibility without deep discounts upfront.

I’ll draft a short internal rubric for approving credit exceptions (> $75k requires Marcus sign-off).

-rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit.rao@prospectco.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: retroactive credits & compatibility concessions

Amit —

Thanks for sharing the incumbent offer. We ran numbers and wanted to propose an alternative that keeps total economic value aligned but reduces your operational risk:

Proposal (summary):
- Migration credit bucket: $120,000 applied across first three invoices; credits redeemable for invoices or services (non-refundable).
- Technical support: dedicated onboarding engineer for 8 weeks + 3rd-party adapter review included.
- Pricing packaging: 10% discount on consumption unit price for the first 6 months if you commit to a 12-month minimum spend threshold (outlined in the attached term sheet).
- Performance safeguard: 30-day compatibility validation window; if the shim work can't be completed, we’ll extend the migration credit by one billing cycle and provide a one-time SLA credit (service credit, not cash).

We believe this preserves the economics of your incumbent offer while aligning incentives for a smooth migration. If this looks reasonable, we can route a one-off credit exception for Marcus to sign and get a DocuSign ready.

Next step: quick call Monday to finalize wording and DocuSign link?

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Pilot_KPI_SLA_Draft.docx

From: Amit Rao <amit.rao@prospectco.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sood <priya.sood@prospectco.com>, Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@prospectco.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: retroactive credits & compatibility concessions

Lauren / Stephanie —

Appreciate the rapid response and the framing. The migration-credit bucket plus the support package gets us most of the way there. A couple of clarifying items before we sign:

1) Can the migration credits be used to offset third-party integration costs (we sometimes bring contractors)? We’d like flexibility but understand limitations.
2) What specific metrics will you use during the 30-day compatibility validation (latency P95, KV hit-rate, error-rate thresholds)? Please list thresholds in the SLA doc so our infra team can sign off.
3) We’d like to preserve a short right of audit on invoices where credits are applied (one-time, within 90 days) to validate proper application.

If you can confirm these quickly we’ll route to procurement today. We’re targeting a signature by this Friday.

Thanks,
Amit
VP, Cloud Platform — ProspectCo
